key_insight: Player-1 proposes learning game-playing agents from synthetic experience, aiming to improve control over visually rich and dynamic environments without relying only on massive human demonstrations. The core idea is to make training more scalable by generating useful experience rather than collecting it all from real gameplay.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the difficulty of training computer-use agents for games, where dynamic states, diverse mechanics, and limited demonstration coverage make data collection expensive and incomplete.
method: Use synthetic experience to expand the diversity of training data beyond what is available from human demonstrations.
Train a game-playing agent to learn from generated interactions that better cover rare or hard-to-reach game states.
Target scalable interactive learning for complex visual environments where manual rollout collection is costly.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more scalable path to training agents for complex digital tasks like games and computer use. It could reduce dependence on large human-labeled datasets while improving robustness in unfamiliar or dynamic situations.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing real gameplay data vs. synthetic experience generation

Game screen + keyboard/mouse action icons to represent computer-use control
Training loop illustration showing synthetic rollouts feeding agent learning
paper_title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
paper_authors: Mingyu Ouyang, Yiran Wang, Siyuan Hu, Xingyilang Yin, Huiqiang Sun
